negative_findings.description: Despite searching in Hungarian for aggregate online cash-register statistics (NAV online pénztárgép összesített adatok, készpénzes/kártyás tranzakció statisztika), no evidence was found that NAV publishes an open aggregate series of cash-register turnover split by payment mode. All located NAV cash-register data services are scoped to the individual taxpayer's own registers.
negative_findings.result_summary: NAV's M2M cash-register download exists but is per-taxpayer; no public payment-mode aggregate located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single richest potential HU cash-vs-card dataset appears to be non-public; obtaining it would require an FOI (közérdekű adatigénylés) or a research agreement, which changes the collection plan fundamentally.

negative_findings.description: No standalone STADAT table dedicated to payment method in retail (kiskereskedelmi forgalom fizetési mód szerint) was found. Payment-method splits appear only inside KSH ICT/e-commerce survey narrative publications, not as a maintained table.
negative_findings.result_summary: Payment-mode data exists in KSH ICT publications but not as a structured, machine-readable STADAT series.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Time-series construction will require PDF extraction rather than table download, and comparability across years must be checked each edition.

negative_findings.description: Searches in Hungarian for a KSH open/JSON API (STADAT API, adatletöltés, nyílt adat) surfaced only the STADAT HTML/XLSX tables and the STATINFO interactive database with a documented ~40,000-cell display limit; no official public REST/JSON statistical API was identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: No confirmed KSH public statistical API found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must assume file-level scraping of XLSX/CSV rather than an API contract, raising maintenance cost and breakage risk.

negative_findings.description: No ÁSZ (State Audit Office) analysis dedicated specifically to cash usage (készpénzhasználat) was located; only adjacent analyses on financial awareness/digitalisation and on tech industry/e-commerce.
negative_findings.result_summary: Adjacent ÁSZ material only; no cash-usage-specific audit analysis found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-claiming ÁSZ as a cash-usage source; it remains a low-priority adjacent watch item.

coverage_gaps.description: Whether NAV would release aggregated, anonymised cash-register payment-mode statistics under a public-interest data request (közérdekű adatigénylés) is unknown and untested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Draft and file a scoped FOI request to NAV for monthly aggregate cash-register turnover and transaction counts split by payment mode and TEÁOR sector; also check the Nemzeti Közadatportál 'igényelhető közadat' route.

coverage_gaps.description: The legal instruments defining online cash register and e-receipt data content (the cash-register decrees and the e-receipt implementing rules) were not retrieved in this pass, so the exact reported fields — including whether payment mode is a mandatory data element — remain unconfirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retrieve the governing decrees from njt.hu / Magyar Közlöny and the NAV eNyugta data-content annexes; confirm the payment-mode field definition and its enumerations.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-register distributor/servicer registers and the population of registered online cash registers by sector (a direct proxy for the merchant acceptance base alongside POS terminals) were not enumerated in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search NAV registers for engedélyezett pénztárgép típusok / forgalmazói engedélyek and any published count of operating online cash registers (üzemeltetett online pénztárgépek száma).

coverage_gaps.description: Ministry-level sources (Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium / Pénzügyminisztérium) and the Magyar Államkincstár were only lightly touched; their fiscal and disbursement statistics (e.g. state payments, treasury cash flows) could add non-central-bank payment signal.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated hu-language pass over nemzetgazdasagi ministry and allamkincstar.gov.hu publication sections.

coverage_gaps.description: Several URLs (KSH publication paths, the Statisztikai Szemle hub, pei.nav.gov.hu) were derived from search result listings rather than direct fetch, so their current liveness and exact paths are unconfirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic liveness pass resolve these; treat 403/timeouts as bot-defence rather than dead, and re-derive paths from the parent topic hubs if a 404 appears.

brief: Hungary's non-central-bank payments telemetry sits in two very different places: KSH, which publishes rich open retail-turnover and household-ICT series but exposes payment-method splits only inside narrative ICT/e-commerce publications rather than as maintained tables; and NAV, which holds by far the deeper asset — receipt-level online cash register and e-receipt data covering practically the whole retail till population, now extending through the e-pénztárgép/eNyugta regime — but publishes no aggregate payment-mode series and scopes machine access to each taxpayer's own registers. The practical collection strategy is therefore open scraping of KSH STADAT (bel* and ikt* families) plus PDF extraction from KSH ICT publications, combined with regulatory monitoring of NAV's eNyugta specification and Online Számla schema to know what fields the state actually captures. The highest-value unexplored move is a formal public-interest data request to NAV for anonymised aggregate cash-register turnover by payment mode, and retrieval of the cash-register/e-receipt decrees to confirm that payment mode is a mandatory reported field.
